Given that the points $A$ and $B$ with coordinates $(6,5)$ and $(-6,-5),$ respectively, are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle centered at the origin, what is the equation of the circle?
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r,$ centered at the origin, is 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

First, we calculate the length of the diameter $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{{(5-(-5))}^{2}+{(6-(-6))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{244} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 61} \\  & =2\sqrt{61}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\overset{―}{AB}$ is a diameter, the radius is

$$
r=\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt{61}}{2}=\sqrt{61}.
$$

So, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =(\sqrt{61})^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =61.\end{aligned}
$$
